prompt:
You receive 5 images. Image 1 is the LAYOUT SKETCH of the finished 1920x1080 game screen: a crude flat-colour blocking that fixes the exact composition - camera, horizon, wall and floor lines, and the position, size and outline of every object. Repaint image 1 into a finished painting: keep every line and every block exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is, paint each block as the object described below, do not move, enlarge, shrink, add or remove anything, and leave no flat colour areas or hard geometric edges. Images 2-4 are photos of the real place (geography, architecture, materials and real details to paint from; they are references only, do not copy their camera, cars, people, signs or weather). Image 5 is a finished background painting from our game: use it ONLY as the reference for the painting technique (brushwork, palette, edge softness, level of detail, line quality); do not copy anything from its scene.

Place: the small measuring room inside a plain brick pump hut on the bank of the Sursky kanal at the edge of Ivanka pri Dunaji, Slovakia, in 1960 - an invented room. Images 2 and 3 are real rooms of the period (type references): image 2 a physics work room with opal globe lamps, a long scale and wooden instrument panels with round dial gauges and switches; image 3 a 1960 laboratory bench with bottles and instruments. Image 4 is the real canal outside (paint it as June: lush grass and reeds) - that is the view through the window. Paint a small, practical, slightly improvised scientific workroom of 1960 from these.

Brief: young Mira works at a table mechanical resonator; a brass calibration plate with four meanings; lamps; boards with invented symbols. 6 June 1960, late afternoon: sunlight through the small window, the globe lamps and the desk lamp are lit, a calm, focused, slightly mysterious mood.

Camera: standing in the room about 1.7 m high, facing the back wall straight on - ONE wall parallel to the picture, vertical lines vertical, no side walls visible; the horizon is at y ~470. Keep this exact geometry from the sketch: the back wall meets the floor at y 720; the long wooden table stands along the back wall from x 560 to x 1360, its top at y 600-622, its legs on the floor at y ~748; the low ceiling beams at y ~60 and ~200.

What the sketch blocks are, left to right: the plank door of the hut at the far left, standing ajar with daylight in the gap; a small wooden window showing the canal, reeds and fields in the sun; a blackboard with chalk drawings of invented symbols - circles, arrows, wave lines and dots, no letters and no digits; on the table: a green enamel desk lamp with a glowing bulb, the table mechanical resonator - a heavy wooden base carrying a row of polished brass rods like tuning forks, a brass cross bar and a small brass pendulum, with the calibration plate on its front - and an open notebook with a pencil; a wooden instrument panel with three round dial gauges and switches on the wall, a cloth-covered cable running down to the resonator; a patch of bare brick; two opal glass globe lamps hanging from the ceiling; a narrow plank door at the right of the back wall with a brass knob; the worn plank floor.

Interactive props - each painted clearly inside its block, the same size as its block, easy to recognise at a glance:
1. the block of the layout sketch at x 866-1024, y 524-612 of the 1920x1080 frame (45-53 % from the left, 49-57 % from the top): a polished brass calibration plate fixed upright on the front of the resonator's base, divided into four engraved fields, each with an invented abstract symbol (no letters, no digits).
2. the block of the layout sketch at x 622-746, y 462-610 of the 1920x1080 frame (32-39 % from the left, 43-56 % from the top): a green enamel desk lamp with a jointed arm and a glowing incandescent bulb, standing on the table.
3. the block of the layout sketch at x 1118-1304, y 566-616 of the 1920x1080 frame (58-68 % from the left, 52-57 % from the top): an open notebook lying on the table with lines of pencil notes, several crossed out (illegible scribbles), and a pencil beside it.
The door at the left is the area of the layout sketch at x 60-230, y 430-720 of the 1920x1080 frame (3-12 % from the left, 40-67 % from the top); the narrow door at the right is the area of the layout sketch at x 1640-1800, y 430-720 of the 1920x1080 frame (85-94 % from the left, 40-67 % from the top).

Walkable floor: the band at x 20-1900, y 735-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (1-99 % from the left, 68-94 % from the top) is the worn plank floor - one continuous flat surface with no step, no rug and nothing standing on it: no chairs, no stools, no boxes, no cables. Only light, shadows and the board joints.
NPC zone at x 1395-1535, y 489-840 of the 1920x1080 frame (73-80 % from the left, 45-78 % from the top): an animated character sprite will stand here later, so paint only plain, uncluttered background in it - no person, no figure, no silhouette, no clothes on hooks that read as a person. The character's feet stand on the floor at y 840.

Fiction rules: entirely invented equipment; no crucifix, no portraits, no posters, no school desks, no brand names, no lettering, no digits anywhere (dials have plain tick marks only). No people, no animals.

The layout sketch is a blocking aid only: paint over all of it. Do NOT draw frames, borders, outlines or boxes around objects, and keep no flat colour block. The finished picture contains no UI, no captions, no text except what is asked for above, no watermark and no people or animals unless stated above.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
